While most fitness applications focus on capturing long-duration cardio activities (e.g. running) and measuring heart rate, WurQ automatically recognizes single movements in the gym environment, measures the volume of physical work done, and assesses its quality (workout log, movement form, strength, effort, output efficiency, pacing). This data helps users access personalized training feedback, avoid injury, and track progress without the need for a qualified coach.

companies.name: xDot Medical Inc.
companies.description: xDot Medical is a medical device company developing the xCinch Access Management system for vascular access. This technology allows for bloodless access site management, reliable closure, and easy re-access to the site to reduce bleeding complications.

companies.name: XO Technology Inc.
companies.description: XO Technology (XO) has developed an AI-powered senior health assessment platform packaged in a discreet ring that continuously monitors functional performance, capturing both biometric and manual motion data. XO offers a novel approach to one of the most pressing challenges in elder care: monitoring and maintaining the functional health of older adults in a way that is scalable, objective, and integrated into real-world care environments. XO’s platform supports smarter, earlier interventions, helping older adults stay independent longer and giving caregivers the information they need to deliver safer, more effective care.

companies.name: Xpan Inc.
companies.description: Xpan is developing a miniaturized access port (trocar) for minimally invasive surgery, which can enter the body at a smaller, less invasive size than current standard devices before expanding to larger, desired sizes, with minimal tissue trauma. This aims to increase safety and efficiency of minimally invasive surgeries.

companies.name: Xylyx Bio
companies.description: Xylyx is a regenerative medicine company that uses its patented XC™ Platform to bioengineer human organ grafts (lung, liver, kidney, heart) for clinical transplantation to save patient lives, increase hospital transplant volume, and save payer costs associated with end-stage disease. In contrast to biofabricated tissue constructs and xeno (animal) organs, the company is addressing the critical shortage of organs for transplantation by bioengineering human, whole organ grafts that provide human anatomic and immunologic compatibility. The company has completed IND‐enabling studies that demonstrate feasibility, efficacy, and safety.

companies.name: Yotta
companies.description: Yotta is developing a modular battery storage device, SolarLEAF™, that integrates with a solar powered/photovoltaic installation on commercial buildings, in remote or inefficient grid areas and in off-grid applications.

companies.name: ZebraKet
companies.description: ZebraKet provides software to optimize inventory stock level recommendations in the supply chain industry. Maintaining the right inventory level and purchasing schedule is critical to reducing tied-up capital, as companies struggle to meet fluctuating demand resulting in a surplus or shortage of goods. ZebraKet’s solution aims to provide improved results compared to traditional methods, with faster and cheaper implementation compared to competitors using classical machine learning methods.

companies.name: Zero Energy Water
companies.description: Zero Energy Water (ZEW) has developed a novel membrane for seawater desalination that replaces existing reverse osmosis membrane technology. As access to freshwater becomes increasingly scarce, the market for seawater desalination is increasing dramatically. Unfortunately, the amount of electricity required in the desalination process is so high that even wealthy countries struggle with the cost of producing fresh water for their citizens. This leads to desalination typically only being used for drinking water, with other needs such as agriculture, industry, and sanitation being neglected. Using ZEW’s patented membrane technology, the cost of desalination can be reduced by up to 90%, dramatically expanding the addressable market for desalination by making it economically viable for agricultural and manufacturing purposes.

companies.name: zerothird GmbH
companies.description: zerothird is developing a pan-European physical infrastructure for quantum key distribution using entanglement-based QKD. Today’s cryptographic keys are distributed over classical channels that can be intercepted, stored, and later decrypted once quantum computers mature, while conventional QKD systems are limited to about 100 km and require dense chains of trusted nodes. zerothird’s approach enables secure key delivery over distances up to 350 km per segment with far fewer nodes, offered through a managed key-as-a-service platform that integrates with existing encryption systems.

companies.name: ZuriQ
companies.description: ZuriQ is developing a scalable trapped-ion quantum computer using a novel 2D ion confinement approach. Unlike competitors constrained by 1D architectures, ZuriQ’s technology enables true 2D grids of ions, offering superior scalability and control. Spun out of ETH Zurich’s quantum computing research, ZuriQ aims to accelerate the path to quantum utility by rapidly increasing qubit numbers in the trapped-ion modality.
